messages.subject: packages psych and lavaan
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to simulate a bifactor model with schmid-leiman orthogonalization, using the packages lavaan, psych, GPArotation and simsem.
My code is the following:
om <- omegaSem(cov(data1), nfactors=3, lavaan=TRUE, n.obs=200, sl=TRUE)
sls.model <- om$omegaSem$model$lavaan
SimSLS1fit200 <- sim(1000, sls.model, n=200, generate=popModel, lavaanfun = "cfa", std.lv=TRUE)
summary(SimSLS1fit200)

I have the following message and some troubles to run the code.
> library(simsem)
Loading required package: lavaan
This is lavaan 0.6-1.1153
lavaan is BETA software! Please report any bugs.

Attaching package: ‘lavaan’

The following object is masked from ‘package:psych’:

    cor2cov

 
#################################################################
This is simsem 0.5-14.903
simsem is BETA software! Please report any bugs.
simsem was first developed at the University of Kansas Center for
Research Methods and Data Analysis, under NSF Grant 1053160.
#################################################################

Attaching package: ‘simsem’

The following object is masked from ‘package:psych’:

    sim


What should I do to overcome this issues?
I really appreciate that someone helps me. Thanks in advance!

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: packages psych and lavaan
parts:
As Ed says, it's not an issue in your case.  It's just saying that both simsem and psych have a function called sim().  

But it can become an issue, when you have some code that uses a function, and then you load another library, which has a function with the same name. If you didn't know about this, you might happily load the psych package, and use the sim function. Then you load the simsem package, and use the sim() function again - but now instead of using the psych function, it uses the simsem function, which is kind of different.

The way around this problem is to always reference the package that the function came from. That also makes it easier for other people reading your code to understand what you did (or when you come back to it in the future). You do this by writing:
package::function()

So your code would (if I got it right) look like:

om <- psych::omegaSem(cov(data1), nfactors=3, lavaan=TRUE, n.obs=200, sl=TRUE)
sls.model <- om$omegaSem$model$lavaan
SimSLS1fit200 <- simsem::sim(1000, sls.model, n=200, generate=popModel, lavaanfun = "cfa", std.lv=TRUE)
summary(SimSLS1fit200)  

Jeremy
